title_guess: Housing Price Index (HPI): what it is, who uses it (buyers, sellers, brokers, lenders, economists, government) and India's two main indices (NHB RESIDEX and RBI's HPI)
recurring_cast: house (one modern house icon, kept at the left from 29 s to 217 s, then faded behind the HPI badge)
line_chart_icon (grey circle with a red zigzag price line, the HPI badge; its line wiggles all the time)
hub of user labels around the badge (buyers, sellers, money lenders, economists, policy makers) with green tick_marks
brand_logo pair for the two index makers (housing bank and central bank)
running_examples: hook: a real listed company's share at about 2,544 rupees with its recent price chart (shown 2,544.95 INR; chart axis 2,300-2,800, Sept-Dec 2022, not spoken)
seller not in a hurry sees HPI down and postpones the sale (spoken only)
buyer defaults, bank sells the house; if bought above the area rate, the sale does not cover the loan (spoken only)

best_moments.why: the share chart shrinks aside and the same question is rewritten for a house beside a house icon: a known tool (price chart for shares) carried over to a new market, so the term arrives as the answer
house -> arrow -> a round badge with a price line, then the name and a one-line definition: the index pictured as 'the price line of houses'
users of the index sit as spokes around the badge and each gets a green tick as it is explained: a cheap progress tracker for a list
the badge sits over a faded house with two maker logos under it, each sending an arrow to its index name with a [2007] tag: one idea, two producers

weak_moments.why: the hook uses a real company's share quote and price chart (brand, real price, real dates); BIE must use a made-up company and avoid anything that reads as buy or sell advice

the red line inside the HPI badge wiggles on a loop for about 250 s; it moves at random and does not fall when 'HPI abhi down hai' is said (70 s), and it hides every real change from the change detector
the seller's example (no hurry, HPI down, postpone, avoid loss) is spoken over an unchanged canvas and a four-line paragraph
a photo of a real man in a film-villain look is labelled BROKER: a real person and a stereotype of a profession
the bank-loan story (loan, documents held, default, sale, shortfall on an overpriced house) runs about 50 s with only a green tick added: the clearest mechanism in the video is never drawn
primary vs secondary market is only in two callout boxes and speech; developer -> buyer vs owner -> new buyer is never drawn

verify before reuse: NHB is called the home-loan regulator (regulation of housing finance companies moved to RBI in 2019); the screen's split (NHB = primary and secondary sales in many cities, RBI = only primary sales in major cities) may not match how the two indices are built (RBI's is usually described as built from property registration data in about ten cities; NHB RESIDEX from bank valuation data and developer prices)

segments.teaches: hook: a share costs about 2,544 rupees today; is this the right time to buy it?

elements.what: real listed company's name, logo and exchange ticker in a stock-quote card
share price '2,544.95 INR' beside the name (not changed, only shown)
serif question over the card: is this the right time to buy this stock? with an underline

segments.notes: 3 change events, each with its word (company name 1.2 s, price 3.4 s, question 6.6 s, about 2 s before the question is spoken). Real brand and price: not reusable.
segments.idea: before buying something whose price moves, you ask whether now is a good time
segments.shown_as: a stock-quote card fades in with the company name, then its price; a serif question 'right time to buy this stock?' writes on above it

segments.teaches: a chart of the share's price over the last few months helps the decision; almost nobody invests without looking at one

elements.what: real line chart of the share price over about four months, pink fill under a red line, price axis 2,300-2,800, month labels

segments.notes: 1 change event; the chart appears 2.7 s before 'ye chart'. Axis values and dates are never spoken. Real data chart: BIE must draw its own made-up series.
segments.idea: a price chart is the usual tool for deciding when to buy
segments.shown_as: a red price line with a pink fill draws under the quote card, rising and falling over a few months; nothing on it is pointed at

segments.teaches: the same question for houses: is there a chart that tells whether this is the right time to buy a house?

elements.what: quote card and chart shrink to a small panel at left; the question fades
question rewritten at right: is this the right time to buy a house?
modern two-storey house under the new question
share panel cleared; the house slides left and a short arrow starts to its right

segments.notes: 3 change events. The house and its question appear about 2.7 s before 'ghar' is spoken. After 36 s the change detector reports one continuous change to the end (the line inside the HPI badge loops), so later segment times are read from the 10 s keyframes and the transcript and are approximate.
segments.idea: houses need the same kind of price chart that shares have
segments.shown_as: the share card and its chart shrink into a small panel at left while the question is rewritten for a house beside a house icon; then the share panel is wiped and the house slides left with an arrow pointing to the space where the answer will appear

segments.teaches: yes: such a chart exists, the Housing Price Index (HPI), a statistical measure of changes in the value of residential real estate over time

elements.what: grey circle badge with a red zigzag price line, at the end of the arrow from the house
'(HPI)' over the badge and HOUSING PRICE INDEX beside it
blue box: statistical measure of changes in the value of residential real estate over time

segments.notes: Times approximate (10 s keyframes). The badge's red line keeps redrawing in different zigzags from here to the end.
segments.idea: HPI is the price line of houses over time
segments.shown_as: the arrow from the house reaches a round badge with a red price line; '(HPI)' and HOUSING PRICE INDEX write on beside it and a blue box gives the one-line definition, while the line inside the badge keeps wiggling

segments.teaches: HPI helps buyers and sellers: knowing whether house prices are up or down lets them decide well; a seller in no hurry who sees HPI down can wait and avoid a loss

elements.what: two short lines from the badge down to 'Buyers' and 'Sellers'
four-line paragraph: buyers and sellers use HPI to sense the market and decide whether to buy or sell

segments.notes: Times approximate. The canvas does not change during the seller's example (63-77 s); the badge line happens to show a dip and a rise, unrelated to the words.
segments.idea: a buyer or seller who knows the price trend makes a better deal
segments.shown_as: two short lines drop from the badge to the words Buyers and Sellers and a paragraph writes on under them; then the picture stays as it is while the narrator tells the seller's wait-and-avoid-loss example
segments.example: seller not in a hurry + HPI down -> postpone sale -> avoid loss (spoken only)

segments.teaches: brokers often quote inflated prices and buyers without information lose; HPI gives a rough idea of what a house should cost, so you are not cheated

elements.what: photo of a real moustached man in a film-villain look, labelled BROKER, beside the house

segments.notes: Times approximate; the photo fades in around 80-89 s, near 'brokers involved'. Nothing shows an inflated price tag or a comparison with HPI.
segments.idea: the index protects you from a middleman's inflated price
segments.shown_as: a villain-like photo marked BROKER fades in beside the house; the rest of the canvas (badge, buyers, sellers, paragraph) stays unchanged

segments.teaches: HPI is not only for buyers and sellers: money lenders, economists and policy makers use it too

elements.what: HOUSING PRICE INDEX (HPI) moves to the top left; definition and paragraph removed
green ticks under Buyers and Sellers
three more spokes from the badge: Money Lenders, Economists, Policy Makers

segments.notes: Times approximate. Buyers and sellers are ticked as 'done' when the narrator says HPI does not help only them.
segments.idea: many kinds of people rely on the same index
segments.shown_as: the title moves to the corner and the text clears; buyers and sellers get green ticks and three new spokes, money lenders, economists and policy makers, branch out around the badge

segments.teaches: money lenders (banks and financial institutions) give home loans and keep the house documents; if the buyer defaults the bank sells the house; if it was bought above the area rate the sale does not recover the loan, so banks check HPI before lending

elements.what: green tick beside Money Lenders

segments.notes: Times approximate; the tick appears between 120 and 130 s, near 'money lenders'. About 50 s of loan-default reasoning with no further visual change.
segments.idea: a bank checks the house price against the area trend because the house is its security if the loan goes bad
segments.shown_as: only a green tick appears beside Money Lenders; the hub stays still while the whole loan, default and resale story is told
segments.example: loan -> documents held by bank -> default -> bank sells; overpriced house -> sale falls short (spoken only)

segments.teaches: economists use HPI to study how consumers behave when house prices rise or fall; government adjusts economic policy because housing is a key part of the economy and shows its health; brokers use it to serve clients and build trust

elements.what: green ticks added in turn beside Economists, Policy Makers and the BROKER photo

segments.notes: Times approximate; each tick falls inside the 10 s keyframe window of its spoken user (economists about 176-180 s, government about 190-199 s, brokers about 205-209 s). Speech says 'sarkar' where the screen says Policy Makers.
segments.idea: the same index also serves research, policy and the trade
segments.shown_as: the hub stays as it is and a green tick lands beside each remaining user as it is explained, ending with a tick over the broker photo, so every spoke is ticked

segments.teaches: India has many housing price indicators; the two main ones are NHB's RESIDEX (NHB described as the home-loan regulator) and RBI's Housing Price Index (RBI is the central bank); both were created in 2007

elements.what: HPI badge enlarged over a faded house, title HOUSING PRICE INDEX (HPI) under it
two blue tiles: the national housing bank logo and the central bank emblem, captioned 'Indian home loan regulator' and 'Indian central bank'
arrows out to 'NHB Residex' at left and 'RBI's Housing Price Index' at right
'[2007]' under each index name

segments.notes: Times approximate. Real logos: BIE must draw generic institution buildings (rbi_building, bank_building). Verify NHB's role (regulatory powers over housing finance companies moved to RBI in 2019).
segments.idea: in India two public bodies publish the main house price indices
segments.shown_as: the canvas clears to the HPI badge laid over a faded house; two institution tiles slide in under it and each sends an arrow outward to its index name, and a [2007] tag drops under both

segments.teaches: NHB's index uses primary and secondary market transactions in different cities; RBI's uses only primary market transactions in major cities; primary = developer sells to buyer, secondary = an owner resells

elements.what: speech box over NHB Residex: based on transactions in primary and secondary markets of different cities (key words highlighted yellow)
speech box over RBI's index: based on primary-market transactions of major cities (highlighted)

segments.notes: Times approximate (left box by about 250 s, right box by about 260 s, each near its words). Primary vs secondary is defined in speech only (258-273 s). Verify the coverage claims before reuse.
segments.idea: the two indices count different kinds of house sales
segments.shown_as: a speech box with highlighted words drops over each index name, the left one saying primary and secondary sales in many cities, the right one primary sales in major cities; nothing shows a developer or a resale

segments.teaches: channel end card (next video / playlist); not teaching

elements.what: next-video and playlist panels with loading bars and an app promo

segments.notes: ignore for teaching; start time approximate (between 270 and 280 s)
